html:
A battle near Nicomedia in northwest Anatolia in which Osman I beat a Byzantine army under Georgios Mouzalon. Most historians date it to July 1302; some give 1301.

The Byzantine force was small and partly made of hired troops. Its defeat showed that Emperor Andronikos II could no longer hold the Anatolian countryside. Turkish raiders and settlers moved into Bithynia, and Osman's small principality became a name that drew warriors from across the frontier.

Bapheus is often counted as the moment the Ottoman state really began. The Byzantines answered by hiring the Catalan Company, which fought the Turks and then turned on its employers. The Bithynian towns fell one by one over the next decades: Bursa in 1326, Nicaea in 1331 and Nicomedia itself in 1337.
sum: A battle near Nicomedia in northwest Anatolia in which Osman I beat a Byzantine army under Georgios Mouzalon. Most historians date it to July 1302; some give 1301.
